h1: 48 Metro Hotel — Rooms Bigger Than the Price Suggests, Bangkok's Lat Phrao Budget Gem
intro: Lat Phrao Wang Hin Soi 48 sits in the quieter northeast stretch of Bangkok — and 48 Metro Hotel has quietly earned one of the best guest scores in its price bracket. With 28 rooms renovated in 2021, free parking, a gym, and a 7-Eleven practically at the front door, it appeals to travelers who want comfort without paying city-center premiums. Score: 8.4/10 from 557 Trip.com reviews. Rates start from approximately ฿600–฿1,100/night depending on room type and season.

body.html: If you need a base in northeastern Bangkok — around the Lat Phrao Wang Hin and Ratchadaphisek corridor — and your budget is under ฿1,200 per night, 48 Metro Hotel deserves a serious look. The property was renovated in 2021 and has 28 rooms managed by a small, attentive team. Guests repeatedly call the staff "friendly" and "genuinely helpful." The name might imply metro-adjacent convenience, but be clear: the nearest MRT station (Lat Phrao) is about 3 km away. A Grab takes roughly 10 minutes. For car-driving travelers, that's a non-issue — there's free parking on-site.

The rooms are the standout. The Deluxe King Room is noticeably spacious for the price point — clean floors, a properly cold air conditioner, and a comfortable king bed. The Two-Bedroom Suite works well for families or groups of three, though it comes with only one bathroom, which is worth knowing before booking if everyone needs to get ready at the same time. The One-Bedroom Suite with two single beds suits pairs who want separate sleeping arrangements.
"The room was spacious, very clean, and the staff were super friendly. Free parking was a bonus we didn't expect at this price."

The immediate neighborhood is surprisingly convenient for daily life. A 7-Eleven is steps from the entrance. A Max Value 24-hour supermarket is nearby. Plaza Lagoon, a small local mall, is about a 5-minute walk. Street food options within a short walk include noodle shops, rice and chicken stalls, and small cafes — all at local prices, not tourist-markup prices. This stretch of Lat Phrao NE is a real residential neighborhood where life happens, and for budget travelers who prefer eating and shopping like locals, that's an underrated advantage.

A few genuine drawbacks to factor in: soundproofing between rooms is reported as thin by several reviewers — a noisy neighbor in an adjacent room will be heard. The Wi-Fi requires a voucher code that expires every two days; if you forget to renew it at the front desk, you'll lose connectivity in the middle of the night. Breakfast is basic self-service — functional, not memorable. And the parking lot can fill up on busy evenings, so call ahead if you're arriving late.

For travelers with city-center MRT-dependent itineraries, the 3 km gap to the nearest station is a genuine friction point. But for anyone visiting for business in Ratchadaphisek or Lat Phrao, or simply wanting a comfortable base to explore this long northeast corridor — from Chokchai 4's night markets down to The Mall Bangkapi — the location makes sense. Grab rides to Central Plaza Lat Phrao and Union Mall (the BTS/MRT interchange at the top of the corridor) run about 15 minutes and rarely cost more than ฿80–100.

The bottom line is straightforward: 48 Metro Hotel delivers more room than the rate suggests, a reliable 8.4/10, and useful extras like free parking and a gym. It is not glamorous, and the MRT gap means you need wheels or a Grab budget. But for a no-fuss, genuinely clean, value-oriented stay in northeast Bangkok, the 557 guests who rated it positively have made a reasonable case.

honestSummary: 48 Metro Hotel is a solid pick for travelers who need a spacious, clean room with free parking in northeast Bangkok and don't depend on daily MRT access. The 8.4/10 score is earned. But the MRT distance and thin soundproofing are real trade-offs worth factoring into your decision.
honestChecks: If you plan to use MRT daily — the nearest station is 3 km away; you'll need a Grab or taxi every time. Consider a hotel closer to a station if MRT access is essential.
If you're a light sleeper — soundproofing between rooms is on the thin side. Request a high-floor room or one away from the corridor; note this when booking.
If you're arriving by car after 9 pm — the parking lot fills up. Call the hotel a day ahead to reserve a space, as front desk is open 24 hours and can hold one for you.

faq.q: Where is 48 Metro Hotel located in Bangkok? Is it near the MRT?
faq.a: 48 Metro Hotel is at 8 Lat Phrao Wang Hin Soi 48, Ratchadaphisek, Bangkok. The nearest MRT station (Lat Phrao, Blue Line) is approximately 3 km away — about a 10-minute Grab ride. The hotel is not within walking distance of the MRT, so it suits drivers or Grab users best.

faq.q: What is the price range at 48 Metro Hotel?
faq.a: Rates start from approximately ฿600/night for a Deluxe King Room, rising to around ฿1,000/night for the Two-Bedroom Suite. Prices vary by date and availability — compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does 48 Metro Hotel have free parking?
faq.a: Yes, parking is free for guests. However, spaces are limited. If arriving late in the evening, call the hotel a day before to reserve a space — the front desk is staffed 24 hours.

faq.q: How is the Wi-Fi at 48 Metro Hotel?
faq.a: Wi-Fi is free, but the voucher system requires renewal every 48 hours. Collect a fresh voucher from the front desk before it expires to avoid losing connectivity at an inconvenient time.

faq.q: Who is 48 Metro Hotel best suited for?
faq.a: Best for budget-conscious travelers who have a car or are comfortable using Grab, and who need a spacious, clean room in the Lat Phrao–Ratchadaphisek corridor. Ideal for business visitors to the area or those seeking a multi-night base without paying city-center rates.
